subject.title: [Feature]:  Missing Session Management Commands in OpenClaw

question: What public session lifecycle contract should OpenClaw expose for stop, kill, pause, resume, and resource limits across Gateway, CLI, and Control UI?
rationale: Current main has partial abort, delete, cleanup, compact, list, UI archive/delete, and admin HTTP subagent kill primitives, but the requested lifecycle controls affect authorization, child-process ownership, persisted session state, UI semantics, and possible resource policy/config defaults.

options.title: Design Additive Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Add guarded Gateway methods plus CLI and Control UI affordances while preserving current abort/delete behavior and documenting upgrade semantics.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Canonical Items
options.body: Keep this umbrella open and route child process kill, topic UI, resume/fork, and diagnostics to focused linked issues or PRs before building the full contract.

options.title: Defer Broad Controls
options.body: Keep current primitives and document limitations until maintainers are ready to own a complete lifecycle and resource policy.

recommendation.title: Design Additive Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Add guarded Gateway methods plus CLI and Control UI affordances while preserving current abort/delete behavior and documenting upgrade semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across the central session Gateway, protocol, CLI, UI, and docs surfaces that the decision would need to coordinate.
